articles.headline: Ravens' Rio trio: The players who helped Jackson to walk-off win
articles.description: Here are the other three players who overcame adversity to help Jackson produce one of the wildest finishes in Ravens history.
articles.body:
Inside the Baltimore Ravens' emotionally charged locker room in Rio de Janeiro, quarterback Lamar Jackson wanted to deliver a message following Sunday's 34-31 walk-off win over the Dallas Cowboys.

"We had all this adversity going on and we conquered," Jackson told his teammates. "This is the start of the season right here."

Jackson and the Ravens redeemed themselves by battling back after letting another fourth-quarter lead disappear, which is a trend that has haunted this franchise for years.

Last week, Jackson's interception sealed a fourth-quarter collapse to the New Orleans Saints. On Sunday, after Baltimore failed to hold an 11-point lead, Jackson put the Ravens in position to win by throwing a pass that traveled 36.4 yards in 1.6 seconds, according to NFL Next Gen Stats.

With only seven seconds remaining on Sunday, he didn't take a knee to run out the clock in regulation and instead threw a 27-yard pass that set up Tyler Loop's winning, 56-yard field goal as time expired. 

"I was prepared for overtime," Ravens linebacker Roquan Smith said, "and then Mr. Houdini [Jackson] made the play."

Here are the other three players who overcame adversity to help Jackson produce one of the wildest finishes in Ravens history:

Tyler Loop

Leading up to Sunday's game, rookie punter and holder Ryan Eckley came up with an idea.

"You know what would be sick is if we hit a game winner," Eckley said. "We go knee-slide in the end zone."

Loop replied, "Dude, there is no way. I feel like I am going to face-plant."

After drilling his first career winning kick, Loop sprinted to the opposite end zone as the entire team raced after him. Then, at one of the most storied soccer stadiums, Loop struck the Cristiano Ronaldo signature celebration in which he jumps and lands with arms outstretched while shouting "Siu!"

The Ravens showed their support for Loop as he lined up for the kick. Jackson yelled encouraging words from the sideline, where teammates felt Loop was going to come through.

"I thought he was going to make it," running back Derrick Henry said. "I wasn't even doubting [anything]. I knew he was ready; I could just tell."

Loop's finest moment in the NFL came after a tumultuous offseason. His only previous attempt at a game-winning field goal came in last season's finale, when his 44-yard field goal went wide right and ended the Ravens' season eight months ago. Then, after Loop's uneven preseason, the Ravens signed kicker Jake Moody to the practice squad as competition.

Now, after Moody was cut earlier this month, Loop has solidified himself with the Ravens, making 5 of 6 field goals (83.3%). This was the Ravens' first winning field goal from 50 yards or longer since September 2021, when Justin Tucker's 66-yarder beat the Detroit Lions.

articles.headline: Warriors' Kristaps Porzingis out with 'health issue'
articles.description: Kristaps Porzingis will miss the start of Warriors training camp because of a health issue.
articles.body:
SAN FRANCISCO -- The Golden State Warriors will be without starting center Kristaps Porzingis to open training camp because of a "health issue," general manager Mike Dunleavy announced.

The Warriors are keeping the details private and calling Porzingis' absence indefinite. He will not travel with the team to Hawaii, meaning he will miss at least the first four practices and the preseason opener against the LA Clippers next Sunday in Honolulu.

"I'm not marking him down as being out to start the season or anything like that," Dunleavy said. "He's just not available this week."

This has been a recurring issue for Porzingis, who has missed a combined 90 games the last two regular seasons primarily because of a mysterious health problem that emerged after he experienced a prolonged upper respiratory viral illness while with the Boston Celtics in late February 2025.

Porzingis missed 10 of his first 11 games with the Warriors after they acquired him from the Atlanta Hawks at last February's deadline, but did return and appear in 16 of the final 21 games.

That, in part, motivated the Warriors to bring Porzingis back this summer on a two-year, $40 million deal, guaranteeing only $3 million in the second season to maintain flexibility next summer.

There was internal optimism about how Porzingis looked this summer. He was in the team's San Francisco facility and on the court in the last week and appeared to be cleared for training camp before Dunleavy received a call on Sunday night about Porzingis' latest health issue.

"He's been participating in everything," Dunleavy said. "It just kind of popped up."

The Warriors are already without starting wings Jimmy Butler III and Moses Moody to enter the season. Both are in the middle stages of extended rehab for serious knee injuries.

"We feel comfortable with everything (about Porzingis' status)," Dunleavy said. "Disappointed that he won't be out there tomorrow, but it's early, so don't want to overreact to anything."

The 2026-27 NBA season officially kicked off Tuesday as the Houston Rockets held their media day, before the Dallas Mavericks followed suit Friday.

The other 28 teams in the association will join them Monday, ahead of training camps beginning for most teams Tuesday.

How will LeBron James and Jaylen Brown look in their new Philadelphia 76ers uniforms? What will Giannis Antetokounmpo's first media day away from Milwaukee look like? And how will the other new faces in new places make their first impressions?

Check back here for all the latest buzz, news and reactions from our ESPN NBA insiders, with the latest info at the top:

Sept. 28

Wembanyama addresses last year's Finals loss

After leading by double digits in each of the five games in last season's NBA Finals, San Antonio Spurs center Victor Wembanyama said his memories of it will fuel the team this season.

"I couldn't imagine a better motivation," he said.

Harper addresses role for coming season

After offseason chatter about his role, San Antonio Spurs guard Dylan Harper said he'd follow the coaches' lead this season.

"Everyone has a competitive edge to them. But the biggest thing for me is whatever I can do, just like last year, to help the team win," he said. "Whatever position the coaches think is best for me to be in, that's the position I'll happily go in."

First look at LeBron in a 76ers uniform

New Philadelphia 76ers forward LeBron James is taking questions from reporters on Monday. Here's what he had to say when asked about his initial impressions of his team:

"Everybody is on the same page," James said. "We are all speaking the same language."

LeBron addressed his role too, saying he's open to whatever the team needs from him to win.

"Whatever they need me to do," he said. "The luxury of my game is I can do everything. ... Literally, I can do everything"

Kawhi: I was a distraction, ready to move forward

In his first public appearance with the Toronto Raptors after a controversy-filled summer, Kawhi Leonard addressed the NBA's investigation into him and his business dealings.

"I know why some of you guys came. You want to hear about the investigation. But in talking with the NBA and PA, I think the best decision is to move forward and focus on my time being a Toronto Raptor," he said. "I already was a distraction for the past 70 days and wasn't able to meet my teammates or do any of that stuff, minicamp stuff, so, moving forward, I just want to talk about the Toronto Raptors."

Haliburton: I am 100% healthy

Indiana Pacers guard Tyrese Haliburton said Monday that he is healthy and ready for the season.

"I am healthy. I am 100%," he said. "There will be no restrictions. That is not news. There is no source. I am the source. I am ready to go for the year."

articles.headline: Source: Packers signing veteran O-lineman Mekhi Becton
articles.description: Veteran offensive lineman Mekhi Becton is signing with the Packers, a source told ESPN's Jeremy Fowler on Monday.
articles.body:
Veteran offensive lineman Mekhi Becton is signing with the Green Bay Packers, a source told ESPN's Jeremy Fowler on Monday.

Becton becomes the second veteran addition to the Packers' offensive line, joining guard Laken Tomlinson, who the Packers signed off the Dallas Cowboys' practice squad.

The Packers have struggled to produce a running game and to protect quarterback Jordan Love due to injuries on the offensive line. Guard Aaron Banks has missed two of the first three games due to injuries and right tackle Zach Bako-Bewele suffered a season-ending torn patellar tendon in Week 2.

Becton was a free agent after the Los Angeles Chargers released him in the offseason, one year after signing him to a two-year, $20 million contract in 2025.

The six-year veteran battled injuries throughout the 2025 season and voiced his frustration with the Chargers at one point last November.

The 6-foot-7, 363-pound Becton appeared in 15 games -- 14 starts -- last season with the Chargers. However, he ranked as the 49th-worst guard in pass block win rate (91.2%) and the third-worst lineman (127th) in run block win rate (63.4%).

Becton, 27, played just 72% of snaps in 2025 and played 100% of snaps in only six games. He missed two games, one with a concussion and another because of a knee injury. (Becton sat out the Chargers' final regular-season game with other starters.) He was also regularly rotated in games; a move the team said was to protect him from injury.

A first-round draft selection of the Jets in 2020, he struggled through four injury-plagued seasons playing offensive tackle in New York before enjoying a revival in 2024 with the Super Bowl champion Philadelphia Eagles, who moved him to guard.

ESPN's Kris Rhim contributed to this report.

articles.headline: NBA preview 2026-27: Stacking the 8 most intriguing newcomers
articles.description: A full roster's worth of NBA stars changed teams this past summer. The storylines surrounding eight will help define the league's journey to spring.
articles.headlineJa: 2026-27 NBAプレビュー：最も注目すべき新加入選手8選
articles.descriptionJa: この夏、ロースター1チーム分に相当するNBAスター選手たちが移籍しました。そのうち注目の8人を巡るストーリーが、春までのリーグの行方を決定づけるでしょう。
articles.body:
There will be plenty of familiar faces donning new jerseys on Monday when NBA media days unfold from coast to coast.

LeBron James and Giannis Antetokounmpo headline a group of six 2026 All-Stars who changed zip codes this summer. In all, 15 players with at least one All-Star selection in the past five seasons are set to take the court for new franchises. (This number includes Anthony Davis and Damian Lillard, who changed teams last season but have yet to play due to injuries.)

To make sense of all that furious player movement, let's run through the eight most intriguing newcomers for the 2026-27 season.

Note: These rankings consider each player's talent, his fit with his new team and other factors such as contract implications and championship expectations. Rookies have been excluded from this list.

1. Giannis Antetokounmpo, Miami Heat

Granted, Antetokounmpo's move to Miami didn't generate as much discussion as Luka Doncic's 2025 trade to the Los Angeles Lakers or LeBron James' latest decision to sign with the Philadelphia 76ers. Yet the two-time MVP deserves top billing from an intrigue standpoint; he was easily the best player to change teams this summer.

In fact, the "Greek Freak" was the only player in the top 12 of this year's NBA Rank who didn't return to the team he played for in 2025-26. And despite an injury-plagued final campaign in Milwaukee, the 31-year-old Antetokounmpo is still in his prime and was an All-NBA First-Team selection in 2024-25.

For those reasons, Antetokounmpo should face real championship expectations. He's about the same age as Shaquille O'Neal was when he joined the Heat in 2004, a move that paid off with a title two years later. Reaching the Finals at some point over the next four years seems like a reasonable benchmark for Antetokounmpo given that Jimmy Butler III led Miami to that stage in 2020 and 2023.

From a basketball standpoint, the Heat must continue building around a pair of star big men in Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo -- a strategic dilemma that's rare for contenders in the pace-and-space era.

Both players possess enough versatility to function together at a high level, but their partnership is bound to look different from any of Antetokounmpo's old Bucks teams or past editions of Adebayo's Heat. Miami could prove to be imposing, clunky or both.

Finally, Antetokounmpo's decision to virtually eliminate the 3-point shot from his scoring arsenal will make him a fascinating test case as he progresses through his 30s. The league's most successful elder statesmen in recent years include James, Kevin Durant, Stephen Curry, Kawhi Leonard, James Harden and Chris Paul, all of whom relied on the outside shot to extend their primes.

Is it possible to age gracefully and avoid recurring injuries while plowing through defenders on a nightly basis? Or will the Heat help Antetokounmpo discover useful adjustments that extend his prime and his team's championship window?

articles.headline: AJ Dybantsa named cover athlete for 2026 Topps Flagship Basketball
articles.description: The Washington Wizards star began collecting cards this year and will be the cover athlete of 2026 Topps Flagship Basketball.
articles.body:
Fresh off being the top pick of the 2026 NBA draft, AJ Dybantsa was named cover athlete of 2026 Topps Flagship Basketball, the company announced on Monday. Pre orders are set to be available on Oct. 6. 

The Washington Wizards rookie never imagined being on a Topps cover, he told ESPN. 

"Topps has been in the business for such a long time, putting out cards before I was born," the 19-year-old told ESPN. "So the fact that I'm a cover athlete, I don't take it lightly. I'm very grateful and appreciative for it."

(Image courtesy of Topps)

Dybantsa is the second consecutive top overall pick to be the cover athlete, with Dallas Mavericks star Cooper Flagg getting the honors last year. Flagg and Dybantsa are both from the New England area: Flagg from Newport, Maine, and Dybantsa from Boston.

Their shared region is something the Wizards forward pointed out when reflecting on following Flagg up.

"Us both being from New England, just putting on for our side of the map," he said. "The northeast doesn't get a lot of love, other than tristate, in my opinion. So us both being from New England, trying to put on for the cities, it feels good."

The Topps Flagship Basketball boasts 20 cards per box with 12 cards per pack. The collection is headlined by a strong 2026 draft class. Following Dybantsa, Darryn Peterson went No. 2 to the Utah Jazz, Cameron Boozer went No. 3 to the Memphis Grizzlies and the Chicago Bulls took Caleb Wilson at No. 4.

Autographed cards of rookies, as well as of veterans and legends, are included. There are also new inserts, including a first-ever Gold one-of-one All Kings parallel, according to Fanatics.

And Dybantsa is the face of it, following a year where his interest in collecting cards grew. When he started signing cards, he started collecting, too, and even has two of himself -- one he bought at Fanatics Fest in July and the other he pulled randomly.

Once the Wizards selected him with the top pick in June, Dybantsa walked on stage, shook NBA commissioner Adam Silver's hand and headed to ESPN's set for an interview. By the time he took his seat, his first NBA rookie card was made. Dybantsa then signed it live on air.

"It was crazy. I don't even know how they did it, to be honest," he said. "I just took the picture, walked the stage. I don't know how they got the card that fast, but it was super exciting. ... I hope to get it one day, but someone else might."

Being a Topps cover athlete should presumably give Dybantsa the upper hand on securing the card. It would only be appropriate, especially since his interest in having his own card has intensified.

Attending Fanatics Fest added to that desire.

"You end up going to that little area where they sell all the cards. And then you just have people bidding, people bidding for my card and it's like now I want to get into it," he said. "I want to collect my own card. So the dude was actually able to help me out and get my first signed card."
